does: Cooks small pasta straight in the broth it will be served in, without draining, so that the broth takes up a little starch and the pasta takes up the flavour of the broth.

intro.what: The broth is both the cooking water and the soup.
intro.why: The pasta's starch thickens the broth a little, and nothing is drained or lost.

how: Bring a well-flavoured broth to a simmer and taste it for salt; there is no extra salted water.
Pour in the small pasta and stir so it does not stick.
Keep it at a gentle simmer, stirring now and then, until the pasta is just tender.
Take it off the heat a little early: it goes on softening and soaking up broth in the bowl.

cues.text: The pasta swells and the broth turns slightly cloudy.
The pasta is tender with no hard centre.

mistakes.mistake: Boiling it too long, so the pasta swells to mush and drinks the broth.
mistakes.fix: Stop just before it is done and serve at once.

mistakes.mistake: Salting as for pasta water, so the broth is too salty.
mistakes.fix: Taste the broth and salt it as a soup.

quiz.question: Why is the pasta cooked in the broth and not in water?
choices: So it takes up the flavour and the starch thickens the broth.
quiz.because: Nothing is drained; flavour and starch stay in the bowl.

quiz.question: How should the broth be salted?
quiz.because: It is eaten, so it is salted as a soup.

quiz.question: When do you take it off the heat?
choices: A little before the pasta is done.
When the pasta is soft and swollen.
quiz.because: It keeps softening in the bowl.

quiz.question: The pasta had swollen and drunk most of the broth. What would you change?
choices: Cook it a little less and serve it at once.
quiz.because: Small pasta keeps soaking after the heat is off.

variant_of.differs: The pasta cooks in the seasoned broth it is served in, salted as a soup and never drained, where boiled pasta cooks in plenty of salted water that is poured away.
